title.sl: Kar je bilo prej: had gone
title.it: Ciò che è venuto prima: had gone

rule.sl:
Ko že govoriš o preteklosti in je nekaj bilo še prej: **had** + deležnik, za vse osebe enako: **When we got to the stop, the bus had already gone.** (Ko smo prišli na postajo, je avtobus že odpeljal.) Slovenščina reče tu preteklik in *že*.

Kratko **'d**: **She'd gone.** Pred deležnikom je 'd had, pred osnovno obliko would (**I'd like**). Zanikano: **We hadn't eaten.** Vprašanje: **Had you seen it before?** V pisanju je deležnik, **I'd gone**, čeprav nekateri rečejo *I'd went*.

**by the time** (dokler, ko že): **By the time we got there, the bus had gone.** Pogosto z **already**, **just**, **never … before**: **I'd never seen the sea before.**

Dve stvari: **When I got home, Sam left.** (potem) **When I got home, Sam had left.** (prej). Kar poveš po vrsti, ostane v past simple: **I got up, fed the dogs and left.**

Z **after** in **before** je vrstni red že povedan, zato je prav oboje: **After she had fed the hens, she went in.** **After she fed the hens, she went in.**
rule.de:
Wenn du schon von der Vergangenheit sprichst und etwas noch davor war: **had** + Partizip, für alle Personen gleich: **When we got to the stop, the bus had already gone.** (Als wir zur Haltestelle kamen, war der Bus schon weg.) Immer had, auch wo Deutsch *war gegangen* sagt.

Kurz **'d**: **She'd gone.** Vor dem Partizip ist 'd had, vor der Grundform would (**I'd like**). Verneint: **We hadn't eaten.** Frage: **Had you seen it before?** Geschrieben steht das Partizip, **I'd gone**, auch wenn manche *I'd went* sagen.

**by the time** (bis, als schon): **By the time we got there, the bus had gone.** Oft mit **already**, **just**, **never … before**: **I'd never seen the sea before.**

Zwei Dinge: **When I got home, Sam left.** (danach) **When I got home, Sam had left.** (davor). Was der Reihe nach kommt, bleibt im past simple: **I got up, fed the dogs and left.**

Mit **after** und **before** ist die Reihenfolge schon gesagt, also geht beides: **After she had fed the hens, she went in.** **After she fed the hens, she went in.**
rule.it:
Quando parli già del passato e qualcosa è venuto ancora prima: **had** + il participio, uguale per tutte le persone: **When we got to the stop, the bus had already gone.** (Quando siamo arrivati alla fermata, l'autobus era già partito.) Sempre had, anche dove l'italiano dice *era partito*.

Forma breve **'d**: **She'd gone.** Prima del participio 'd è had, prima della forma base would (**I'd like**). Negativo: **We hadn't eaten.** Domanda: **Had you seen it before?** Per iscritto si usa il participio, **I'd gone**, anche se qualcuno dice *I'd went*.

**by the time** (quando ormai): **By the time we got there, the bus had gone.** Spesso con **already**, **just**, **never … before**: **I'd never seen the sea before.**

Due cose: **When I got home, Sam left.** (dopo) **When I got home, Sam had left.** (prima). Ciò che racconti in ordine resta al past simple: **I got up, fed the dogs and left.**

Con **after** e **before** l'ordine è già detto, quindi vanno bene tutti e due: **After she had fed the hens, she went in.** **After she fed the hens, she went in.**
rule.en:
When you are already talking about the past and something came earlier still: **had** + the participle, the same for every person: **When we got to the stop, the bus had already gone.**

Short **'d**: **She'd gone.** Before a participle 'd is had, before a base form would (**I'd like**). No: **We hadn't eaten.** To ask: **Had you seen it before?** Writing wants the participle, **I'd gone**, though some people say *I'd went*.

**by the time**: **By the time we got there, the bus had gone.** Often with **already**, **just**, **never … before**: **I'd never seen the sea before.**

Two things: **When I got home, Sam left.** (afterwards) **When I got home, Sam had left.** (earlier). What you tell in order stays in the past simple: **I got up, fed the dogs and left.**

With **after** and **before** the order is already said, so both are right: **After she had fed the hens, she went in.** **After she fed the hens, she went in.**

rows: by the time + past simple, had
By the time we got there, the bus had gone.
When I got home, Sam left.
After she fed the hens, she went in.
